clue.text: Leaving work in recording studio?

definitions.meaning: setting off or departing in a hurry, an idiom for heading away
laying down the separate musical recordings that make up an album

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for setting off, and literally producing songs for a record, two senses of one phrase.

clue.text: Dish for rock star

definitions.meaning: a baked dish of minced beef shaped into a block
the stage name of the American singer of Bat Out of Hell

explanation.definitionFit: A minced-beef bake shares its name with the American rock singer famous for Bat Out of Hell.

clue.text: Effect of lullaby in Stevenson's book?

definitions.meaning: a lullaby leaves a young child (a kid) having napped

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes a dozing child; it is also the title of Stevenson's novel of abduction.

clue.text: A small drink for each child

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
per means for each, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: Someone orders one small drink apiece for the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is informal British slang for a small child.

clue.text: Beery film or article by bad actor in Communist Party

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: in places the bad actor inside the party's abbreviation

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overplays

explanation.surface: Talk of a beer-soaked movie or a story about a hammy actor in the Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beery' looks like 'boozy' but is Wallace Beery, who starred in the 1931 boxing film.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallace Beery won an Oscar for the lead in this 1931 boxing film, so it is a Beery film.

clue.text: Investigator transported in our helicopter

indicators.note: transported suggests carried off to a new place, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A detective is flown somewhere in our helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian detective is a fictional investigator.

clue.text: City that's elegant — one with vitality

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
a means one, as in 'a dozen'
go means energy or vitality, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: Praise for a stylish, lively city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illinois metropolis on Lake Michigan is a major American city.

clue.text: A shaft at right angles to a vessel

definitions.text: at right angles to a vessel

parts.note: a beam or shaft of light

explanation.surface: A ray of light strikes the side of a ship squarely.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for a position level with a ship's middle, perpendicular to its keel line.

clue.text: Spanish inn or post office seen by small girl

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Choosing between a Spanish hostelry and the post office a little girl visits.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is the Spanish word for an inn or lodging house.

clue.text: A doctor of divinity at college has to make sense

parts.note: DD is the degree abbreviation for Doctor of Divinity
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A theologian at university needs to be logical.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: when an argument hangs together and is consistent it adds up.

clue.text: Jacket — 75% less — that is not smooth

parts.note: a jerkin is a sleeveless jacket

indicators.note: 75% keeps the closing three of the four letters of the word less

explanation.surface: A jacket at a steep discount turns out to be rough.
explanation.walkthrough: '75% less' looks like a sale price; it means three quarters of LESS, i.e. ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerkiness is a quality or motion that is abrupt rather than smooth.

clue.text: Kipling's work is only a plea for help, right?

parts.note: just means only, as in 'just a minute'
SOS is the distress signal
the Tories are the political right in Britain

explanation.surface: Asking whether Kipling's writing amounts to nothing more than a cry for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party, the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's 1902 collection of children's origin tales is one of his works.

clue.text: For sale — fantastic footwear

indicators.note: fantastic suggests fanciful or unreal, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: An advert praises shoes on sale as fantastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafers are slip-on leather shoes, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Defenceless as Venus in the Louvre

definitions.meaning: the Venus de Milo statue in Paris famously lacks arms

explanation.definitionFit: Without weapons, and literally without arms like the famous armless statue.

clue.text: Snakes, when extremely poisonous

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of the word poisonous

explanation.surface: A warning about snakes being highly venomous.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, the Egyptian cobra among them.

clue.text: A drug for a traveller in space

parts.note: a steroid is a drug, e.g. used by athletes

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drug to prepare an astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky body moving through space, so a traveller there.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, one chapter on Hegel's interpretive method

parts.note: a dialect is a regional way of speaking
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remark about a chapter that discusses Hegel's philosophical reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel's philosophy proceeds by thesis, antithesis and synthesis, known as his dialectic.

clue.text: Lots of wealth dedicated to music?

parts.note: for means intended for or devoted to
tunes are pieces of music

explanation.surface: Lots of money devoted to music.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortunes are large sums of money, i.e. lots of wealth.

clue.text: Many soldiers vote in parliament

definitions.meaning: an army formation of several brigades
a formal count in the Commons where members file into lobbies

explanation.definitionFit: A large army unit, and the British parliamentary vote by lobbies.

clue.text: Bog-standard comprehensive and a civic centre erected

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in this down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: all-in means inclusive or comprehensive, as in an all-in price

indicators.note: centre points to the middle letter of the word civic

explanation.surface: A dismissal of an ordinary state school and a council building put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' suggests a British state secondary school; here it is ALL-IN. Upward reading of ALLIN + A + V gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is slang for plain or ordinary, just like bog-standard.

clue.text: Such a lorry needs a headlight

indicators.note: needs here means requires inside itself, so the letters sit within the phrase

explanation.surface: A truck of that type must have a headlamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headlight' suggests a lamp on the lorry; it is a light round a saint's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light painted round a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Italian flower girl's first memory of persecution

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word girl's

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: A girl's earliest recollection is of Italian flowers and persecution.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is an organised massacre or persecution of a group.

clue.text: Extremely cold beer

definitions.meaning: a British draught ale with a hoppy taste

explanation.definitionFit: Describes a biting wind, and is a type of British ale.

clue.text: Gibbons in vacation destination

definitions.meaning: the Florida city famous for theme parks

explanation.definitionFit: First name of composer Gibbons, and the Florida holiday city.

clue.text: Sort of early bird producing eggs

definitions.text: Sort of early bird producing eggs

parts.words: Sort of early bird producing eggs
parts.note: a hen kept for its eggs, which is up at dawn

explanation.definitionFit: A hen bred for egg production is called by this name.

clue.text: Wear and tear round object

indicators.note: round means the tear encloses the object

parts.note: a rent is a tear in fabric
an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: Clothes suffer wear and tear around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is old-fashioned word for clothing, i.e. what one wears.

clue.text: Whence change changed normality?

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking where the change to normal life came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' means coins: the place they come from.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mint produces British coins, so loose change comes from there.

clue.text: Put it another way, a little giant

indicators.note: a little means only a small part of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: A request to rephrase something, a small giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans were giant gods of Greek myth, so the word means a giant.

clue.text: Darkness surrounds chap on seafront in Russian port

indicators.note: surrounds puts the darkness around the man and the S

parts.note: murk is gloom or darkness
man means a chap
the front of the word sea is S

explanation.surface: A man by the sea is lost in gloom in a Russian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmansk is an ice-free port in north-west Russia.
